sources.note: Only three references: Lama 2012 (subclassification), Bradley 2007 pp. 396-397 (comments), Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment). No descriptive source of any kind; Glottolog 5.1 export in shows Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.

sources.note: Wordlist pages exist for Nasu (Lanqing), Nisu (Dao San), Yi (Kunzhai), Ku varieties; no Chesu page.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Shuangbai County', 'Xinping Yi and Dai Autonomous County', 'List of lesser-known Loloish languages' (raw wikitext)
sources.note: Ethnographic only: Shuangbai County Gazetteer 双柏县志 (1996: 89-90) lists Chesu 车苏 2,528 at Candoutian 蚕豆田, Hekou 河口乡, Damaidi, Yulong, Ainishan; Xinping County Gazetteer 新平县志 (1993: 106, 118) lists Chesu among Yi subgroups; the lesser-known-Loloish list notes 'the Chesu claim that their language is not a Yi language'.

No phonology beyond the autonym transcriptions tsu su33 pa21 (Yunnan 1955 云南民族识别参考资料 p. 40) and tɕi21 su55 pho21 吉输颇 (Long Luogui 龙倮贵 2007, 红河彝族族源族称及其人口分布); cites Bradley 2007 Encyclopedia chapter (Nasoid; being replaced by Nisu and Chinese) and Ethnologue (3,300 speakers, L2 of Hlersu).

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages: a study from the perspectives of shared innovation and phylogenetic estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp.

sources.note: Chesu occurs only twice, both in name lists (p. 4 list of Nisoic ethnonyms; p. 52 reproducing Bradley 2007's Northern Ngwi inventory 'Aluo.., Chesu, Samei, Samataw..'); no Chesu data, nothing on stress anywhere in the dissertation (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. (supported by David Bradley). 2007. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2007-095: create [ych] Chesu. SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress; justifies a separate code (distinct identity from Northern Nisu; recognised in YXZZ 1994 Yuxi Diqu zhi and by Bradley 2007 'based on fieldwork findings'). Sources cited: Bradley 2007 (Atlas of the World's Languages 2nd ed.), YXZZ 1994; first-hand: 1998 onsite research in Xinping.

sources.note: Nothing on phonology; classification 'Sino-Tibetan, Tibeto-Burman, Burmic, Ngwi (Loloish), Northern', closest language Samatao; 3,300 speakers; written literature/recordings field left blank.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh), 彝语东部方言 (车苏语 redirects here), raw wikitext
sources.note: Phonology section concerns Eastern Yi generally (46 initials, 20 rhymes, four level tones), not Chesu; the only Chesu sentence is '另有车苏等支系，语言上接近东部方言，但是分布在彝语其他方言区内。' ('There are also branches such as Chesu, linguistically close to the Eastern dialect but located in other Yi dialect areas.') Nothing on stress.
